title: US Sets Ukraine-Russia Talks for Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11 as Strikes Continue
dek: Envoy Steve Witkoff announced a working-level trilateral round after last week's localized truce, while Russia's strike on an aid site in Zaporizhzhya killed at least 31 people.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Skyline of Abu Dhabi, the city that will host the US-mediated Ukraine-Russia talks on Nov. 10-11

keyPoints: US special envoy Steve Witkoff said on Nov. 2 that Washington will bring Ukrainian and Russian delegations together in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11 for working-level talks, Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reported.

Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to lead the US side. Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to the trilateral format after meeting Witkoff in St. Petersburg, RFE/RL reported. It would be the first such round since February.
Ukraine said a Russian strike on a school where humanitarian aid was being distributed in Zaporizhzhya on Nov. 2 killed at least 31 people, with nearly 50 still missing, RFE/RL reported.
The Kremlin has said last week's localized truce in Oleshky does not mean Moscow is ready for a wider ceasefire, RFE/RL reported.
body:
The United States will host a new round of Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11, US special envoy Steve Witkoff announced on Monday, Nov. 2. Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reported that the talks will be working-level and focus on what it quoted Witkoff as calling "post-war security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts, and next steps toward peace."

## The talks

Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to represent Washington, a senior US official told reporters, according to RFE/RL. The previous round of US-mediated trilateral talks was held in February, before the war involving the US, Israel and Iran interrupted the diplomatic process.

The Guardian reported in late October that Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready to talk, and that territorial questions would have to be raised at leadership level, while other issues would go to technical groups. Zelenskyy also said Ukraine would not discuss limits on its armed forces or enforced neutrality at the November meeting.

## The fighting continues

RFE/RL reported that the local truce in Oleshky, which allowed residents of the Russian-occupied city to receive aid and evacuate, offered some hope of a wider settlement. The fighting has continued, however. Ukraine said Russia struck a school where humanitarian aid was being distributed in the Zaporizhzhya region on Nov. 2, killing at least 31 people. The regional military head said nearly 50 people were still missing.

On Nov. 3, Russian attacks injured at least 62 people at a medical facility in Kharkiv and damaged energy infrastructure elsewhere, officials said, according to RFE/RL. Zelenskyy said Moscow launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles overnight. Ukrainian drones struck an oil refinery in Yaroslavl, Russia, officials said.

## Energy strikes and the refinery dispute

The Guardian reported in late October that the US has been pressing Ukraine to suspend strikes on Russian oil refineries, which Washington says push energy prices higher. Zelenskyy said Kyiv would stop those strikes only if Moscow stopped hitting Ukraine's power infrastructure, if the US allowed Ukraine to use Starshield satellite internet to detect the launch sites of Russian ballistic missiles, or if Washington supplied Patriot interceptors.

Zelenskyy also said Russia had launched nearly 2,300 strike drones at Ukrainian cities in the week before Oct. 25, along with about 1,600 guided bombs and 48 missiles of various types, and urged Western allies to speed up interceptor deliveries, the Guardian reported.

## What remains open

Ukraine has said it will not discuss limits on its armed forces or enforced postwar neutrality at the November round. Zelenskyy has also renewed his call for a meeting with Vladimir Putin, according to the Guardian's late-October reporting. RFE/RL said the Abu Dhabi talks are aimed at "post-war security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts, and next steps toward peace."

Meridian has not independently verified the casualty counts. They are as reported by Ukrainian officials and RFE/RL.
